images.title: Unfold so the line stays on the net
images.purpose: Show the unfolding of the cuboid where the straight path from the ant to the laddu stays on the net, and its length.
images.composition: One flat net of two faces centred on white with the straight path and its right triangle.
images.exact_structure: Two faces lying flat side by side and sharing one vertical fold line: on the left a 4 cm by 4 cm square (the end face), filled pale teal #0072B2; on the right an 8 cm wide by 4 cm tall rectangle (the long face), filled pale amber #E69F00. The fold line is dashed grey #6B7280. The ant is a dark dot at the centre of the square, 2 cm left of the fold and 2 cm above the bottom edge, labelled 'ant'. The laddu is a dark dot on the bottom edge of the rectangle, 2 cm right of the fold, labelled 'laddu'. A straight thick dark line joins them and stays inside the faces. A dashed grey right triangle sits under the path: a horizontal leg of 4 cm along the bottom edge line labelled '4 cm' and a vertical leg of 2 cm under the ant labelled '2 cm', with a small right angle mark. The path is labelled '√20 ≈ 4.47 cm'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Pick the unfolding where the straight line stays on the net; that line is the shortest path.

images.context: One clean concept image for T9.C2.
images.teaching_notes: Cuboid 8 cm by 4 cm by 4 cm; ant at the centre of an end face; laddu on a long bottom edge 2 cm from that end. √(4² + 2²) = √20.

image_decisions.why: The shortest path is a straight line on the right unfolding; drawing that net shows it.
